_note: Easily confused Chinese words. Each pair gets a page at /pairs-<id>. 'match' tells build.py which corpus tokens count as an example (optional pinyin filter, so 得 de is not confused with 得 dé). Hand examples are shown when the readings have none. 'quiz': true builds fill-in questions from the readings; only for pairs where swapping the word is reliably wrong. Written 2026-09-24.

pairs.title: 预订 vs 预定: book or schedule?
pairs.short: Same sound, different character: booking something vs fixing a plan.
pairs.summary: Both are pronounced yùdìng. 预订 means to book or order something in advance, so it is held for you: a hotel room, a table, tickets, a cake. 预定 means to fix or schedule something in advance: a plan, a date, a meeting time. Rule of thumb: if you are reserving a thing or a service, write 预订; if you are setting a time or a plan, write 预定.
points: 预订
book / reserve / order ahead: 预订房间, 预订机票, 预订座位
预定
schedule / fix ahead: 预定时间, 按预定计划, 预定下周开会

预订: 我在网上预订了一个房间。
周末人多，最好先预订座位。
It's busy at the weekend, so it's best to book a table first.
预定: 会议预定在下周三上午。
The meeting is scheduled for next Wednesday morning.
飞机按预定时间起飞了。
The plane took off at the scheduled time.

pairs.title: 这儿 vs 这里 (and 哪儿 vs 哪里): here and where
pairs.short: They mean the same thing; the difference is where you are.
pairs.summary: 这儿 and 这里 both mean "here"; 那儿 and 那里 both mean "there"; 哪儿 and 哪里 both mean "where". The 儿 forms are typical of northern, spoken Mandarin (Beijing); the 里 forms are more common in the south, in Taiwan and in writing. Use either and you will be understood everywhere. One fixed exception: when someone praises you, the modest reply is 哪里哪里, never 哪儿哪儿.
points: 这儿 / 哪儿
northern and colloquial: 你在哪儿？我在这儿。
这里 / 哪里
southern, Taiwan and written Chinese; also the modest reply 哪里哪里

pairs.title: 栋 vs 座: measure words for buildings
pairs.short: How to say your building and unit, and which measure word goes with a building.
pairs.summary: Both 栋 and 座 are measure words for buildings. 栋 is used for houses and buildings, and in many cities it is also the number of a residential building in a compound: 3栋 is Building 3. 座 is a broader measure word for large, fixed things: buildings, mountains, bridges, towers, even cities (一座山, 一座桥, 一座城市); office complexes often label their towers A座, B座. In an address, 单元 (dānyuán) is the entrance or stairwell of a building, so 3栋2单元501 is Building 3, Entrance 2, Flat 501.
points: 栋
houses and buildings; building numbers in residential compounds: 一栋楼, 5栋
座
large fixed things: 一座山, 一座桥, 一座城市; office towers: A座

座: Our company is on the 12th floor of Tower B.
这座桥已经有一百多年了。
This bridge is more than a hundred years old.

pairs.title: 二 vs 两: two ways to say two
pairs.short: 二 for counting and numbers, 两 before a measure word.
pairs.summary: 二 is the number two when you count, read out numbers or give an order: 一、二、三, 十二, 二十, 第二, phone numbers. 两 means "two of something" and goes in front of a measure word: 两个人, 两本书, 两杯咖啡. With 千, 万 and 亿 both appear, but 两千, 两万 are the everyday choice.
points: 二
counting, digits inside numbers, ordinals: 二, 十二, 二十, 第二, 二楼
两
two + measure word: 两个, 两本, 两次; also 两千, 两万

pairs.title: 会 vs 能 vs 可以: can, three ways
pairs.short: A skill you learned, an ability or circumstance, or permission.
pairs.summary: All three translate as "can". 会 is a skill you have learned (我会说汉语, 我会游泳) and also "will probably" (明天会下雨). 能 is ability or capacity, or whether circumstances allow it (我能游一千米, 今天我不能来). 可以 is permission or "it is possible / OK to" (这里可以拍照吗？). In questions asking for permission, 可以 and 能 overlap: 我能进来吗 and 我可以进来吗 are both fine.
points: 会
learned skill: 会开车; likelihood: 明天会下雨
能
ability, capacity, circumstances: 能吃三碗饭, 今天不能去
可以
permission, it is OK to: 可以坐这儿吗？

pairs.title: 了 vs 过: done, or ever done
pairs.short: Completion or change vs experience at some point in the past.
pairs.summary: After a verb, 了 marks that the action is completed (我吃了早饭), and at the end of a sentence it marks a change (下雨了, 我饿了). 过 marks experience: you have done it at least once at some unspecified time (我去过北京 — I have been to Beijing). Negate 了 with 没 and drop the 了 (我没吃); negate 过 with 没 and keep the 过 (我没去过).
points: 了
completed action: 我买了一本书; new situation: 天黑了
过
experience, have ever: 你吃过火锅吗？ 我没去过上海。

pairs.title: 的 vs 得 vs 地: three particles, one sound
pairs.short: Before a noun, after a verb, before a verb.
pairs.summary: All three are pronounced de. 的 links a description to a noun: 我的书, 漂亮的衣服. 地 turns a description into a way of doing, before a verb: 慢慢地走, 高兴地说. 得 comes after a verb or adjective and introduces how well or how much: 跑得很快, 说得不错, 累得不想动. A quick test: noun after it → 的; verb after it → 地; verb before it → 得.
points: 的
description + noun: 红色的车, 妈妈做的菜
地
manner + verb: 认真地学习, 慢慢地说
得
verb + degree or result: 写得很好, 忙得没时间吃饭

pairs.title: 再 vs 又: again, before or after it happens
pairs.short: 再 for an again that has not happened yet, 又 for one that already has.
pairs.summary: Both mean "again". 再 is for a repetition that has not happened yet: a plan, a request, a suggestion (请再说一遍, 明天再来). 又 is for a repetition that has already happened (他昨天又迟到了), and for things that regularly recur, even in the future (明天又是星期一). 再 also means "then, and only then" (吃完饭再走).
points: 再
not yet happened: 再来一杯, 我们下次再去; then: 做完作业再玩
又
already happened: 他又来了; regular recurrence: 又到周末了

pairs.title: 在 vs 正在: doing it now
pairs.short: Both mark an action in progress; 正在 stresses right at this moment.
pairs.summary: Put 在 or 正在 before a verb to say an action is in progress: 我在吃饭, 我正在吃饭. 正在 puts more weight on "right at this moment". 在 is also the verb "to be at" and the preposition "at" (我在家, 在学校学习), which 正在 is not. Adding 呢 at the end is common in speech: 他在睡觉呢.
points: 在
in progress: 你在做什么？; also at / to be at: 在家, 在北京工作
正在
right now, at this moment: 我正在开会，一会儿给你打电话

pairs.title: 知道 vs 认识: know a fact or know a person
pairs.short: Knowing information vs being acquainted with someone or recognising something.
pairs.summary: 知道 is knowing a fact or a piece of information, or knowing of someone (我知道他叫什么名字). 认识 is being acquainted with a person, having met them, and also recognising something like characters, a place or a road (我认识他, 我认识这个字). You can 知道 a famous actor without 认识 them.
points: 知道
facts, information, knowing of: 我不知道, 你知道他住在哪儿吗？
认识
acquainted with, recognise: 认识你很高兴, 我不认识这个字

pairs.title: 还是 vs 或者: or, in questions and in statements
pairs.short: 还是 when you are asking someone to choose, 或者 when you are not.
pairs.summary: Both translate as "or". Use 还是 in a question that asks someone to pick one option: 你喝茶还是咖啡？ Use 或者 in a statement, when either option is fine: 喝茶或者咖啡都可以. 还是 also means "still" and "had better" (还是早点睡吧), which 或者 never does.
points: 还是
or in a choice question: 你今天去还是明天去？
或者
or in a statement: 周末我看书或者去公园

pairs.title: 有点儿 vs 一点儿: a little, before or after
pairs.short: 有点儿 before an adjective (often a complaint), 一点儿 after it or with a noun.
pairs.summary: 有点儿 goes before an adjective or verb and usually signals something slightly unwelcome: 有点儿贵, 有点儿累. 一点儿 goes after an adjective to compare or ask for a change (便宜一点儿, 快一点儿), or before a noun for a small amount (喝一点儿水). So a shopper says 有点儿贵，能便宜一点儿吗？
points: 有点儿
before adj / verb, often negative: 今天有点儿冷
一点儿
after adj to compare: 大一点儿; before a noun: 一点儿钱

pairs.title: 以后 vs 后来: after, later, afterwards
pairs.short: 以后 works for past and future; 后来 only tells what happened next in the past.
pairs.summary: 以后 means after or later, for the future or the past, and can follow a time or an event: 下班以后, 三年以后, 以后我想去中国. 后来 means afterwards and is only used to tell what happened next in a past story; it stands on its own at the start of a clause: 后来我们成了好朋友. You cannot say 下班后来.
points: 以后
after X, from now on, later (past or future): 吃饭以后, 以后见
后来
afterwards, in a past story: 后来他搬走了

pairs.title: zěn vs zhēn: 怎 and 真, a pronunciation pair
pairs.short: z vs zh and third tone vs first tone, the two differences that keep these apart.
pairs.summary: 怎 (zěn, as in 怎么 zěnme, how) and 真 (zhēn, really) differ in two ways. The initial: z is made with the tongue tip behind the top teeth, zh with the tongue tip curled back behind the gum ridge. The tone: 怎 is third tone (low, dipping), 真 is first tone (high and level). Get either one wrong and 怎么样 can sound like 真么样.
points: 怎么 zěnme
how, why: 怎么走？ 你怎么了？ (z, third tone)
真 zhēn
really, truly: 真好, 真的吗？ (zh, first tone)

pairs.title: 哪 vs 几: which or how many
pairs.short: 哪 asks which one, 几 asks how many (a small number).
pairs.summary: Both go before a measure word. 哪 asks which one: 你要哪个？ 哪天？ 几 asks how many and expects a small number, usually under ten: 你有几个孩子？ 几点了？ For bigger or unknown amounts use 多少: 多少钱？ 你们学校有多少学生？
points: 哪 nǎ
which: 哪个, 哪本书, 哪国人
几 jǐ
how many (small numbers): 几个人, 几点, 星期几
